text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High packet loss observed from POP=syd1 -> upstream-carrier-a; loss >8% for 10m; elevated 5xx and origin timeouts for AUS/NZ customers. Severity: P1. Paging on-call for edge/network.

maya: acked. I'm oncall. jumping in now. any customer hits list? :eyes:

incident-bot: most affected prefixes: 203.11.45.0/24 (large-cdn-cust), 198.51.100.0/24 (playback), aggregated telemetry: edge 5xx up 12x from baseline, cache hitrate down 18% for syd1.

alex: seeing the same in grafana. mtr from syd1-cache-03 to upstream shows packet loss starting at our peering port:
```
Host            Loss%   Snt  Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
192.0.2.10       0.0%    10   1.1   1.2   1.0   2.5   0.5
10.254.1.1      30.0%    10  12.4  13.8  11.2 102.0  28.3
203.11.45.1     85.0%    10 120.2 118.9 110.1 140.5  10.2
```
Looks like loss appears at our egress to carrier-a downstream. Could be peering issue or last-mile carrier congestion.

srini: Can we confirm BGP withdraws/ASN flaps? querying routeviews and our bgp logs now.

netops-bot: Detected BGP session resets with carrier-a from POP syd1 at 2026-03-15T09:05:10Z. Repeated flaps on neighbor 203.0.113.254 -> 5 resets in 7m.

emily: customer support flagged ~6 tickets about intermittent playback errors starting 09:06 UTC.

maya: triage plan: 1) fail traffic away from carrier-a for syd1 to alternate carriers (carrier-b) 2) if BGP unstable, announce more-specifics to steer 3) open timeline in status. Dan, can you run the steering change? @dan

dan: on it. running policy change via traffic API now.

dan: POSTing steer request:
```
curl -X POST https://api.internal.redwood/traffic/steer \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"pop":"syd1","preferred_upstreams":["carrier-b","carrier-c"],"expiration":"15m"}'
```
Response: 202 accepted. new steering id: steer-33a4. Rolling to active in 30s.

alex: confirm BGP shows new communities applied on our routers. also adding temporary more-specific announcements for heavy prefixes to bring them onto carrier-b path.

srini: running connectivity checks to verify egress path. traceroute to 203.11.45.12 now shows path via carrier-b.

alex: early metrics: within 2m after steer applied, packet loss from syd1 -> upstream-carrier-a dropped (we're steering away), overall 5xx rate down ~60% for affected prefixes.

maya: good. keep steering for 30m and monitor. netops, please keep an eye on BGP resets and confirm if carrier-a reports any outage.

netops-bot: Sent notification to carrier-a NOC: ticket #CAC-2026-487. They acknowledged and are investigating congfuration on their peering fabrics. ETA unknown.

emily: drafting status page update: "We are investigating increased errors for customers in Australia and New Zealand; traffic is being rerouted to alternate upstreams to mitigate impact." Will post in 5m and link here.

maya: customer-impact summary for oncall notes: ~12k requests/min affected at peak, error burst lasted ~8m, degraded UX for video playback and large asset delivery. No evidence of data loss.

alex: adding firewall check — no rate-limits/truncation on our side. origin healthchecks are green. issue seems purely in transit.

srini: checking DNS implications: noticed an odd pattern where some DNS queries to our authoritative AS were being answered from a small set of anycast nodes incorrectly due to upstream path shift. Could cause additional cache churn.

maya: that's important — can you expand? are we seeing NX/NODATA or just latency on DNS answers?

srini: mostly long latency and occasional SERVFAIL when packets are dropped. not persistent NX. impact: clients retry and hit different POPs causing cache misses and origin fetches.

dan: mitigation for DNS churn: increasing TTL for edge authoritative responses for 10m to reduce churn and cache fill. applying now.

dan: command:
```
curl -X POST https://api.internal.redwood/dns/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"pop":"global","set_ttl":600,"note":"temporary during syd1 carrier outage"}'
```
Response: OK.

maya: good. keep TTL change for 15m then revert. continue to monitor RUM and SLOs.

netops-bot: carrier-a reports partial fabric degradation affecting peering in ap-southeast2 AZ-B; they propose BGP flap due to a misapplied config. They are rolling rollback.

alex: once carrier-a confirms stable, we'll remove steering and TTL revert. Need a clear signal: BGP session stable for 30m and packet loss <1% at peering.

emily: status update posted: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/syd1-2026-03-15

maya: handing off to alex for post-incident follow-up and RCA once carrier confirms. I'll remain available for customer comms.

alex: ack. I'll own RCA and timeline. initial notes captured. collecting pcap and mtr outputs from affected nodes and saving to /var/tmp/incidents/syd1-2256009999.tar.gz. attaching to incident later.

dan: removing temporary more-specifics now that we see carrier rollback in progress. issuing withdraw for steer-33a4, TTL revert scheduled in 10m.

netops-bot: Carrier-a reports rollback complete at 2026-03-15T09:27:34Z. BGP session resets ceased.

alex: observing packet loss down to <0.5% on peering again, 5xx rates back to baseline. marking mitigation complete.

maya: thanks team. I'll close the pager once alex posts RCA. posting a short postmortem template to fill:
- timeline
- root cause
- mitigation & remediation
- follow-ups (netops: coordinate with carrier to prevent bad config push; infra: add automatic steer triggers; product: notify top affected customers)

alex: will fill RCA and notify stakeholders. Good job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

emily: I'll follow up on the 6 customer tickets and link to RCA when available.

maya: handing off final oncall to srini for overnight monitoring. srini, you good to take it?

srini: taking it. will watch BGP and edge metrics. set pager to low.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation rolled back; monitoring shows stable peering. Incident closed for now. Refer to timeline id=2256009999 for logs and artifacts.
